Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking a look at Carewell's pilot request. We're preparing to run a 6-week clinical triage pilot and need to confirm a few privacy/data-use items before we can proceed: 

- A firm, timeboxed no-training commitment for all pilot data (no model updates, no transfer to third-party model training pipelines).
- Clear ownership/entitlement for prompts and responses generated during the pilot (we expect return of all transcripts + an output license that prevents Redwood from deriving models from our outputs).
- Subprocessor gating: we need pre-notification and written approval for any subprocessor that will have access to raw or cached conversation data; for the pilot we must approve any new subprocessor.
- Onshore residency for logs and any captured telemetry for the pilot (US only).

I've attached a short SOW and a one-page summary of our security requirements. Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet these as part of a pilot engagement and what the operational steps/evidence will look like?

Thanks,

Hi all — operational details we can commit to for the pilot (6 weeks):

- No-training: We'll apply a strict processing flag at the request router that prevents any pipeline that feeds model improvement from seeing pilot traffic. This is an enforced config for the pilot tenant and will be scoped to the pilot dates; no token-level telemetry will be forwarded to training pipelines.
- Data residency: All request/response logs and ephemeral caches will be routed to our US-only secure bucket with restricted access. We can provide a signed attestation and a short runbook describing access control and log retention.
- Subprocessor gating: For the pilot, we agree to a change-control workflow: any new subprocessor that would access pilot data must be disclosed 10 business days prior and requires written approval from Carewell. Existing subprocessors that do not touch pilot-data remain unchanged.
- Evidence: We will deliver: (a) subprocessor inventory export (CSV) for the pilot scope; (b) an access log snippet for one representative day; (c) the attestation that the no-train flag was enabled.

Operational asks for Carewell:
- One technical contact for onboarding (name + email + time zone).
- Expected RPS and avg tokens per request.

Attached: subprocessor_inventory_20280715.csv (csv).

Emma / Kimberly / David —

Thanks — below is the contract-level language we'd propose as a narrow pilot amendment to the DPA. This is intentionally concise so it can be signed quickly and reversed at pilot end if needed. Happy to redline per your counsel.

Proposed amendment (pilot-only, effective dates {pilot_start} to {pilot_end}):
1. No-Training Commitment: For the duration of the pilot, Redwood shall not (and shall ensure its subprocessors do not) use Pilot Data for model training, model fine-tuning, or any process intended to improve or adapt any machine learning model. Pilot Data shall be processed only for the purpose of providing the Services under the Agreement.
2. Output Entitlements: Carewell Health retains exclusive rights to raw prompts and responses generated during the pilot. Redwood grants Carewell a perpetual, worldwide license to export and use captured outputs; Redwood shall not assert any model-derivative rights over such outputs.
3. Subprocessor Approval: Redwood shall provide a current subprocessor list upon execution of this amendment and shall provide notice of any proposed subprocessor who would have access to Pilot Data at least 10 business days prior to onboarding; Carewell shall have the right to reasonably withhold approval.
4. Evidence Deliverables: Within five (5) business days of execution, Redwood shall provide the subprocessor inventory, an attestation of the no-training configuration, and a sample access log covering a representative 24-hour period.

Please confirm whether this form is acceptable or propose edits. Also advise if you need the amendment to reference any specific regs (e.g., HIPAA BAAs) — if so, we'll loop in our security governance team.

I'll draft a short one-page amendment and attach it here.

-Markus
